title: Recently written list sorted by date

history.detail:
PASS: QA1 gate 1, round 1: PASS. Audited commit aca36fb against the current sprint file, re-read fresh. The file is unchanged since 5044e23, and no criterion asserts anything between versions. Sprints 30 and 31 are merged to main and closed, which satisfies the stated dependency.

R1 Met.
- shapeDateNavigation now sorts a copy of the RPC rows with byIsoDateAscending, a code-unit comparison of event_date.
- event_date is a Postgres date that PostgREST serialises as zero-padded YYYY-MM-DD. The app's range is 1700-2100, so every year has four digits and string order is chronological.
- It never sorts on the long-date label and never uses localeCompare.
- Desktop and the phone details list both render the same RecentList from navigation.recent, so both get the order.

R2 Met. Nothing under supabase/ changes. The sort runs in shapeDateNavigation, after loadDateNavigation has read the RPC result. The SQL cap still picks the 20 most recently written before the reorder. The sort works on a spread copy, so the input rows are not mutated, and the test asserts that.

R3 Met. Excluding bookkeeping, the diff is exactly three files:
- lib/date-page/navigation.ts: the sort;
- app/date/[date]/DateNavigation.tsx: a one-line doc comment;
- lib/date-page/navigation.test.ts.
isCurrent, previous/next and the unavailable path are untouched.

R4 Met.
- The new test feeds rows in generation order, deliberately not date order: 1789-07-14 among 1945, 1969 (three months), 2001 and 2012 dates. It asserts exact ascending output and that the current-date marker survives. It also asserts the set is unchanged and the input is not mutated. Its comment shows the label-sort order it would catch.
- Existing tests were changed only for order: the first shape test and the loadDateNavigation success test, where the same entries are reordered. The old "keeps database order" test asserted the behaviour this sprint deliberately replaces, and the new test supersedes it.

Ran these myself:
- npm test: 26 files, 291 tests, green.
- typecheck: clean.
- lint: clean.
- build: clean, /date/[date] dynamic.

No Human Prerequisites. No test was labelled known-failing.
commit=95f4f3d | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for 95f4f3d5a296648c5311c008edaba3ae6cbe898d all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: PASS (round 1). Tested 2026-11-23, about 01:10 UTC, against
https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app.
Shipped commit 95f4f3d. Production serves the pushed tip 92ebca9: /api/health/db reports
status ok and commit 92ebca9. git diff --stat 95f4f3d 92ebca9 touches only
docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json, and so does aca36fb..95f4f3d.
CI: runs 45091664256 (95f4f3d) and 45092192530 (92ebca9). build, rls-tests and migrate all
succeed in both.
Tools: headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57, real clicks) at 1280x900 and at 390x844 with
isMobile, plus curl against Supabase REST with the anon/publishable key.

STEP 1, oldest first on desktop and phone: PASS.
On /date/1984-02-29, 1969-07-20, 1776-07-04 and 2001-09-11, the "Dates with readings" list
reads, in both layouts:
1776-07-04, 1920-08-18, 1929-10-24, 1945-05-08, 1963-11-22, 1969-07-20, 1976-07-04,
1977-08-16, 1986-03-31, 1991-06-12, 2001-09-11, 2021-01-06.
That is strictly ascending, and it mixes the 1700s with 20th- and 21st-century dates and
different months.
On the phone, the summary "RECENTLY WRITTEN (12)" opens to the same 12 items in the same
order. scrollWidth is 390.

STEP 2, same set as the RPC: PASS. POST rpc/get_recent_reading_dates {} with the anon key
returned 12 dates in generation order: 2021-01-06, 1929-10-24, 1991-06-12, 2001-09-11,
1969-07-20, 1977-08-16, 1976-07-04, 1920-08-18, 1776-07-04, 1945-05-08, 1963-11-22,
1986-03-31. Compared programmatically: the sorted RPC set equals the rendered list exactly,
and the RPC order differs from the rendered order. So the rows are the same and only the
order changed.
2021-01-06 is a new qualifying date since Sprint 31 (created 2026-11-23T00:55:51Z,
matchedYear true). It was not cast by LiveQA.

STEP 3, current marker and prev/next: PASS.
The current date is a SPAN with aria-current, not a link, at its sorted position:
- 4 July 1776 first;
- 20 July 1969 sixth;
- 11 September 2001 eleventh.
Prev and next are unchanged in shape:
- 1984-02-29 shows 1977-08-16 and 1986-03-31.
- 1969-07-20 shows 1963-11-22 and 1976-07-04.
- 1776-07-04 shows null and 1920-08-18.
- 2001-09-11 shows 1991-06-12 and 2021-01-06, the new date.
Real clicks from /date/1984-02-29 landed as follows, on desktop and phone:
- "previous reading" went to /date/1977-08-16, h1 "16 August 1977";
- "next reading" went to /date/1986-03-31, h1 "31 March 1986".

No console or page errors.
